newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cogema swaps mining stakes with Cameco.
newsitem.headline: Cogema swaps mining stakes with Cameco.

text.p: French state-owned Cogema said on Thursday that it had agreed to sell its 25 percent stake in Wyoming-based Joint Venture Highland to Cameco of Canada, which already controls the venture through a 75 percent interest.

In exchange, Cameco has agreed to sell Cogema a 20 percent stake in the Kiggavik mining property in Canada's Northwest Territories in which a Cogema subsidiary already holds 79 percent, Cogema, a nuclear materials firm, said in a statement.

Terms were not disclosed, but Cogema said the Kiggavik property's uranium reserves were estimated at around 16,000 tonnes. "A delivery of 308 tonnes of uranium to Cogema will balance out the operation financially," it said.
Cogema said the agreement would allow it to increase its mining activities in Canada, adding that it had some significant holdings in the province of Saskatchewan.
